title: Curatorial Design and Composition: Estar vs Ser + Participle

sections.content:
You know *estar* + past participle for a visible result from B2 Unit 20 (*La puerta está cerrada*, *Los cuadros están dañados*), in contrast with *ser* + participle for an action from B1 Unit 18 (*El camino fue cerrado ayer*). In exhibition reviews, this contrast separates two different layers of an artwork:

• ***Estar* + participle** describes the **current curatorial layout and visual composition**: how a gallery is organised, how lighting is directed, or how a canvas is structured (*La muestra está articulada en tres salas*, *El lienzo está resuelto con trazos firmes*).
• ***Ser* + participle** reports the **historical act** of creation, commissioning, or restoration, especially with a date or a *por* agent (*El lienzo fue restaurado por el taller municipal el año pasado*).

sections.title: Curatorial state vs historical action
rows: La muestra está articulada en cuatro núcleos.
The exhibition is structured into four sections. (layout)
Los bocetos están organizados por etapas.
The sketches are arranged by period. (curatorial state)
El lienzo fue restaurado por el taller en mayo.
The canvas was restored by the workshop in May. (action)
La instalación fue diseñada para este patio.
The installation was designed for this courtyard. (creation)

items.spanish: La curaduría está pensada para avanzar desde los bocetos hasta las obras mayores.
items.english: The curation is designed to move from the sketches to the major works.

items.spanish: La iluminación está dirigida hacia el centro del lienzo.
items.english: The lighting is directed towards the centre of the canvas.

items.spanish: Estas tres telas fueron restauradas por el equipo del museo el invierno pasado.
items.english: These three canvases were restored by the museum team last winter.

items.spanish: La instalación está rodeada de muros blancos que refuerzan su presencia.
items.english: The installation is surrounded by white walls that reinforce its presence.

sections.content: In English, 'is structured' and 'was restored' both use 'be', so learners often pick *ser* for gallery layout (*La sala ~~es~~ articulada en tres partes*). Use *estar* whenever you describe how the exhibition or composition stands before the viewer, and reserve *ser* for the event of making, buying, or restoring it.
